title: Attorney Payment Information Returns
what_to_do: Use the correct tax-year IRS information-return process. Distinguish payment for legal services (potential Form 1099-NEC) from gross proceeds paid to an attorney (potential Form 1099-MISC); the payee, payer, payment type and reporting year control. Gross-proceeds reporting is not a statement of the attorney’s taxable fee. Have the responsible payer verify current instructions, reporting thresholds, taxpayer information and electronic or scannable filing requirements. This route links instructions; it does not generate or file a tax return.

title: Settlement Information Return Selection
what_to_do: Identify each actual settlement component and the responsible payer before selecting the applicable tax-year IRS form. A taxable nonwage payment, attorney gross proceeds, interest and wages can require different reporting; taxable wages use the wage-reporting process. An information return does not decide the recipient’s tax treatment. Use the current official instructions and supported allocation; no return is filled or filed by this route.

title: Clerk Certified Abstract of Judgment
what_to_do: Request the certified abstract from the clerk of the court that entered the judgment and follow the receiving clerk’s docketing requirements. CC-1407 is a service form, not an abstract. A drafted Word document cannot supply the clerk’s certification.

See the /garnishment official-form entry. Include the required exemption notice; a bank-levy letter alone does not levy an account. For another court, use that court’s forms and clerk process.

Certificate of Interested Entities is not a universal Virginia civil pleading requirement. Use the court’s required form and disclose only supported facts for the required persons/entities. Federal and out-of-state disclosure rules need their own review; no generic certificate is generated from this ambiguous command.

title: Select Counterclaim or Crossclaim
what_to_do: Choose the pleading from the relationship between the parties: /counterclaim for a claim against an opposing party under Virginia Rule 3:9; /crossclaim for a qualifying claim against a co-party under Rule 3:10. A claim involving a new third party requires separate impleader/joining analysis. Cross-complaint is too ambiguous to map automatically. Confirm the parties, claim and service requirements before selecting the template.

title: Summons for Judgment Debtor Interrogatories
what_to_do: Use the actual court’s judgment-debtor interrogatory process under Virginia Code § 8.01-506. For Circuit Court, CC-1481 is the official summons; the authorized clerk or commissioner issues it. See the /summons-interrogatories official-form entry. A generic debtor-examination order is not a substitute for issued process.

title: Virginia Default Procedure Selection
what_to_do: In Virginia Circuit Court, Rule 3:19(a) places a defendant in default upon failure to file a timely responsive pleading; do not import a separate federal clerk-entry step. If seeking judgment, use /default-judgment after checking valid service, response time, notice, military-status requirements and proof of damages. A defendant seeking relief follows a different procedure. Confirm the actual court and stage before drafting.

title: Full Demand Package with Exhibits
what_to_do: The source app assembled a demand letter and selected exhibits into one PDF. That feature is not part of this library. Use /demand (or /policylimits) for the letter and /demand-exhibits for the exhibit index; attach the actual records yourself.

title: Select Trial or Post-Verdict Motion
what_to_do: For a Virginia civil jury trial, identify the procedural stage and the ruling sought. The /strike template addresses a motion to strike the evidence under Rule 1:11; a post-verdict /jnov request requires separate statutory and preservation analysis. The federal JMOL label does not choose between them. Confirm the court, evidence closed, prior motions, verdict and applicable deadline before using either template.

Verify the correct procedure for other enforcement or exemption types.

title: Professional Liability and Client Decision Review
what_to_do: Virginia Rule of Professional Conduct 1.8(h) prohibits ordinary prospective limitation of a lawyer’s malpractice liability. Its narrow exception concerns a lawyer’s employer-client independently represented in making the agreement; ordinary independent advice is not a general exception. Do not generate a malpractice protection waiver. If the purpose is to record actual advice and a client’s settlement-planning choice, use /snt-waiver, which does not release counsel; an existing malpractice claim requires separate ethics and legal review.

title: Medical Records Audit Excel Export
what_to_do: The source app exported a spreadsheet audit from its stored medical records. That feature is not part of this library. For an editable summary drafted from actual records, use /medsummary.

title: Obtain Medicare Recovery Demand
what_to_do: BCRC issues the formal recovery demand after the required settlement information and related-payment review. Use /medicare-settlement-report for counsel’s supported settlement report and retain the actual demand when received. The MSPRP final conditional-payment process is a separate, tightly timed option under CMS’s current instructions; an interim conditional-payment amount is not necessarily the final debt. This command does not invent a CMS demand, balance, appeal deadline or clearance.

title: Obtain Medicare Rights and Responsibilities Letter
what_to_do: CMS/BCRC sends the Rights and Responsibilities letter after the case is established in the recovery process. Obtain and retain the letter for the actual beneficiary and case, and follow its current instructions. Use the representation and claim-notification templates (/medicare-bcrc, /medicare-notice) if a case must first be reported. A lawyer-drafted letter cannot be presented as CMS’s RAR letter, and no agency notice is generated here.

title: Medicare Future-Medical Allocation Review
what_to_do: An allocation requires actual medical records, treatment recommendations, prescription information, cost methodology and claim-specific Medicare analysis. A qualified preparer must support those inputs and calculations. Confirm whether this is workers’ compensation or another claim type; CMS’s published WCMSA review process is not a universal liability-settlement approval system. No medical prognosis, life expectancy, allocation amount or CMS approval is generated by this command.

title: CMS Workers Compensation MSA Submission
what_to_do: First confirm that the matter and proposal fit the current CMS workers’ compensation MSA review process. CMS recommends the WCMSA Portal and also describes paper/CD submission. Use the current Reference Guide and complete supported proposal, authorizations and medical/cost records. A cover letter alone is not a submission or approval, and a liability PI case must not be represented as eligible merely because it involves Medicare. This route provides instructions; it does not transmit anything.

title: Select Service Acceptance or Waiver Process
what_to_do: Identify whether the recipient is accepting service, waiving service of a summons, or merely acknowledging delivery. These acts have different effects. For an applicable Virginia waiver request use the official waiver form (see /waiver-service); for actual acceptance use /acceptance-service after confirming the authorized signer and legal effect. Receipt alone is not proof of valid service, and this command does not substitute a California notice-and-acknowledgment procedure.

title: Pooled Special Needs Trust Joinder Review
what_to_do: Obtain the selected nonprofit’s current master trust and joinder. Benefits counsel must review disability, settlor authority, sole-benefit administration, fees, remainder/Medicaid provisions and transfer consequences for the actual beneficiary. Pooled-trust treatment is not identical to the under-65 self-settled trust exception, and transfers after age 65 can still carry penalties. A generic Word joinder cannot enroll a beneficiary in an unidentified provider’s trust.

what_to_do: Coordinate the fund instrument and proposed approval order with the fund administrator and tax counsel. Verify qualifying claims, a governmental order or approval with continuing jurisdiction, segregated assets, administrator powers, distributions, tax reporting and termination. A private agreement alone does not establish every requirement of a qualified settlement fund. The responsible team must supply the actual claims, authority, fund terms and approval route before an operative instrument is prepared.

Qualification under 26 U.S.C. § 130 is not established by the document title. The provider’s terms must match the settlement and any approval order; no assignment is generated or treated as accepted here.

title: Settlement Preservation Trust Design
what_to_do: Identify the beneficiary’s capacity, property, benefits, intended distribution rights, trustee, fees, creditor exposure and tax objectives before selecting a trust instrument. Virginia trust-creation requirements do not by themselves establish benefit protection or asset protection. Have trust counsel prepare or adapt the operative terms and obtain any settlement-court approval. A generic preservation trust must not be substituted for a special needs trust or treated as automatically protecting eligibility.

title: Self-Settled Special Needs Trust Design
what_to_do: Use benefits and trust counsel to prepare the actual self-settled trust. Verify the beneficiary’s disability and age, funding source, lawful settlor, sole-benefit terms, trustee powers, Medicaid reimbursement at death, termination provisions and the requirements of each benefit program. The individual trust exception under 42 U.S.C. § 1396p(d)(4)(A) differs from a pooled trust. Obtain required court approval and program review; the name special needs trust does not establish eligibility.
